result.raw_final:
Yes. An American citizen planning to work in UK healthcare for longer than 6 months will need the appropriate work permission. For an eligible healthcare or adult social care role, the **Health and Care Worker visa** may apply. GOV.UK says you need an eligible job with a Home Office approved UK employer, a confirmed job offer and certificate of sponsorship, and to meet the role’s salary requirements. The visa can last up to 5 years and can be extended if you remain eligible.

The six-month visitor allowance does not permit ordinary employment: Standard Visitors cannot do paid or unpaid work for a UK company. Whether an American needs a separate visa or ETA just to visit is a different question from permission to work.

Sources: [Health and Care Worker visa](https://www.gov.uk/health-care-worker-visa) · [Standard Visitor rules](https://www.gov.uk/standard-visitor)

FINAL ANSWER: Yes. To work in UK healthcare for longer than 6 months, an American citizen needs appropriate work permission, usually the Health and Care Worker visa if the role and applicant meet its requirements. A visitor stay of up to 6 months does not authorize ordinary paid or unpaid work.
